title: 2023 AMC 10A Problem 4
statement: A quadrilateral has all integer side lengths, a perimeter of \(26,\) and one side of length \(4.\) What is the greatest possible length of one side of this quadrilateral?

solutions.text: In any quadrilateral each side is shorter than the sum of the other three. Call the longest side \(s.\) The rest sum to \(26 - s,\) so \(s \lt 26 - s,\) which gives \(s \lt 13\) and hence \(s \le 12.\) Can we hit \(12?\) The sides \(4, 12, 9, 1\) work, since \(12 \lt 4 + 9 + 1.\) So the greatest length is \(12.\) Therefore, the answer is D.
hints: In any quadrilateral, each side is less than the sum of the other three
If the longest side is \(s,\) the other three sum to \(26 - s,\) so \(s \lt 26 - s\)
